statement: dev-intel shows only allowlisted publishers' repos, not every repo named dev-intel-test-0
question: Why doesn't dev-intel show every publisher who pushes to a dev-intel-test-0 repo?
argument: Repo names are per wallet, so anyone can create <wallet>:dev-intel-test-0 and the explorer will index it. With live: true the app would merge all of them, and any record could carry a prompt injection to every agent that reads the network. Pinning live to named wallets (0x<wallet>/dev-intel-test-0) is the one defence that does not depend on detecting the attack. The team's wallets go first; opening to the wider network means adding wallets, and later a trust score from how others' records support or refute a publisher's. Publish-time screens and treating records as data stay as second and third layers.
subject: fangorn

evidence.excerpt: Publishers are an allowlist (`live` per wallet): the team's wallets only to start.
live is true (every repo members push) or a list of the namespaces they push to: "name" (any wallet's) or "0x<40 hex>/name" (that wallet's)

statement: One record type with a kind field (finding, decision, log, claim) instead of a type per kind
question: Why does dev-intel use one record type for findings, decisions, logs and claims?
argument: All four share one shape: a statement, the argument for it, and evidence. One type keeps one role map, so search ranks them together and an agent asking 'why did we pick A over B' also finds the research finding the decision rested on. kind is a facet, so filtering stays cheap. A type per kind would split search into four lists and force every new kind through a schema change; a new kind here is one more value in the source's KINDS list.

statement: Records about private repos are published with the repo name and internal hosts withheld; the reasoning still ships
question: Can an agent publish decisions made in a private repo to dev-intel?
argument: Fangorn has no way to make a record readable only by a team: its private mode lets anyone who pays read. Everything published is public and permanent. So a decision from a private repo is published with an opaque project label instead of the repo name, and no internal URLs or code. The 'chose A over B because' part is what other agents need, and it rarely depends on the repo's identity. The publisher is responsible for what they publish; the source withholds what it can detect (keys, tokens, emails) before staging.
subject: dev-intel

evidence.excerpt: Records about private repos never name the repo or its internal hosts; an opaque label instead.

statement: dev-intel stores to IPFS through Fangorn's storage worker, not a Pinata JWT, until the 1 GB free tier runs out
question: How does a Fangorn publisher upload without a Pinata account?
argument: The fangorn CLI uses a Pinata JWT when one is configured; with none, it asks the storage worker for a one-time signed upload URL, proving the wallet by signing a challenge. Setting signedUrlWorkerUrl in ~/.fangorn/config.json to https://base-sepolia.storage-worker.fangorn.network/ is the whole setup, and reads use the network's default gateway. The worker's free tier is 1 GB; past that, configure your own Pinata JWT and gateway (they must belong to the same Pinata account).
subject: fangorn

statement: westmarch-ship --register --dry-run prints a placeholder <project>.workers.dev URL; the real run binds the URL wrangler deploy prints
question: Will westmarch-ship bind the wrong workers.dev URL on chain?
argument: The dry run never deploys, so it cannot learn the account's workers.dev subdomain and prints https://<project>.workers.dev. The real run parses the URL from wrangler deploy's output and throws if there is none, so the card it binds on chain is the deployed one. Seen on dev-intel-test-0: dry run said dev-intel-test-0.workers.dev, the real run bound dev-intel-test-0.fangorn-0be.workers.dev. If wrangler sees more than one account, set CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID or site.account first.

claims.text: The dry run falls back to https://<project>.workers.dev.
The real run throws if wrangler deploy printed no workers.dev URL.

subject: westmarch

evidence.excerpt: if (!deployed && !dry) throw new Error("wrangler deploy printed no workers.dev URL; set site.url");
